candidats.description: Focus on a bike parked, free-standing, on path in front of a section of facade. The facade is wooden casing and picturesquely worn metal cladding. Low greenery in a flower bed borders where the foundation meets the path. This is Træ building at Jægergårdsgade and Kalkværksvej at Sydhavnen - the Southern Harbour quarter, Aarhus, Denmark. It is 20 storeys and 78 metres high. At the time of construction: Denmark's tallest wooden building. Concrete and glass are also used and lots of the material is reused or recycled. candidats.description: Like a tribute to Gaudí, the Casa Comalat contains many elements of Gaudí's architecture, and is one of the most original examples of home-grown art nouveau in Barcelona: modernisme. Two distinct façades, both of them showing the influence of the curve redolent of the work of the Reus-born maestro, arouse our curiosity to go and take a closer look at this beautiful and unique building. The architect Salvador Valeri i Pupurull worked on the Casa Comalat from 1906 to 1911, and was clearly influenced by Gaudi's organic forms. File:Frank Sickels House, Buffalo, New York - 20200618.jpg
candidats.description: The Frank Sickels House, 119 Oakland Place, Buffalo, New York, June 2020. One of the oldest extant houses on the street, this two-and-a-half-story beauty dates to 1891 and was the design of an unknown architect. The style is a hybrid one: the large frontal gable with the lovingly restored foliate ornamentation at its peak represent the Queen Anne style to the hilt, while the Tuscan columns on the reconstructed porch add a Colonial Revival element to the mix. Original owner Frank E. Sickels (1860-1920) was a Buffalo attorney who was also active as the historian of the local chapter of the YMCA

candidats.description: The Batterson-Kleckner House, 2254 Main Street, Buffalo, New York, September 2020. Built in 1899, the house is a typical example of the Queen Anne architecture that was very popular around the turn of the century and which is the predominant style in the Parkside East Historic District. Interesting features that deviate somewhat from the stylistic norm include the hipped roof, the front portion of which descends from the façade from a false gable and ends in a moderately overhanging eave, as well as the rugged-textured concrete block that comprises the pilasters supporting the porch roof. candidats.description: The Charles and Florence Sears House, 75 Barker Street, Buffalo, New York, June 2020. Quite the anachronism: the house owes its Federal design (a style that had been out of fashion for nearly three-quarters of a century at the time of the house's construction in 1914) to the owner's fancy for a house he'd seen while on a seaside vacation in New England (some sources specify Nantucket); he commissioned architects Bley & Lyman to design an exact replica. candidats.description: The Henry R. Clark House, 94 Oxford Avenue at West Balcom Street, Buffalo, New York, October 2020. candidats.description: The Hatmaker-McDonnell House, 493 Woodward Avenue at Crescent Avenue, Buffalo, New York, September 2020. Located in the Frederick Law Olmsted-designed Parkside East Historic District, the Hatmaker-McDonnell House was described by the Buffalo Friends of Olmsted Parks in 1984 as "the finest example of a Queen Anne-style residence on Woodward Avenue". The detailing here is truly remarkable, with all the requisite characteristics of the style shining brightly: the turret is round and topped with a bell-shaped roof; the Classically-inspired front porch features a handsome balustrade, Doric pilaster
